context_purpose: A landlord wants to know whether the tenant's household qualifies for a discounted water rate so the shared-meter bill split is computed correctly.

norm_violation_today.reason: A prior-address bill discloses old address, usage volumes and arrears to a landlord who only needs a rate-class fact.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing material for the bill split; the landlord cannot see arrears or past usage, which could matter to a cautious landlord but is not the stated purpose.

transmission_check.reason: No law is known to oblige a private landlord to collect a prior water bill; it is an informal request.

context_purpose: A platform wants an estimate of a vendor's turnover to set a deposit or credit limit for merchant onboarding.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full personal and business statements expose customer names, family transfers and private spending far beyond a turnover band.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Mixed cash and informal transfers make deposit bands understate turnover, and the platform cannot see concentration or chargeback-like patterns.

transmission_check.reason: The platform's risk screening is a business choice rather than a statutory duty, so a narrower attestation is allowed if it accepts it.

context_purpose: A multi-employer benefits or commuter-subsidy operator needs to confirm that a user is currently employed at an enrolled firm so only eligible staff get the benefit.

norm_violation_today.reason: An HR letter or staff card photo reveals name, title, department and sometimes pay when only active status is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The operator loses the ability to see role or department, which it does not need for eligibility; a stable account key must still be separately handled.

transmission_check.reason: The employee hands documents over voluntarily to receive the benefit, with no known duty to keep the full letter.

context_purpose: A parent, platform or small school wants assurance that a person who will be alone with children is not on the sexual-offender registry.

norm_violation_today.reason: A full criminal-record certificate exceeds a registry-absence question, but where child-protection rules apply the employer may be entitled to see it.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The narrow proof omits other relevant convictions (violence, abuse offences outside the register) that a hiring side may legitimately care about, and may give false comfort.

transmission_check.reason: For regulated child-related roles the employer may be obliged to check specific records, though informal parents and platforms are not clearly under that duty; I cannot confirm the exact rules.

context_purpose: A care facility or kindergarten wants to keep infectious disease out of a vulnerable population by confirming a visitor or staff member is currently cleared.

norm_violation_today.reason: The whole lab report discloses ID number, other tested items and hospital visit details when only a cleared status is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Little for door screening; an auditor or health inspector may want the underlying record, which a status proof does not give.

transmission_check.reason: Facilities may be told by health authorities which records to keep for inspection, and I cannot confirm whether a signed status would satisfy that.

context_purpose: A housing office wants to confirm the rented unit is billed at the residential rate with its own meter before granting a rent subsidy.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full bills expose usage, landlord or account-holder name and unrelated charges beyond a tariff-class fact.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The office still needs the address and tenant link to administer the subsidy, and a roll-membership proof alone does not tie the account to the applicant.

transmission_check.reason: The applicant submits bills voluntarily to receive the subsidy, but a public body may have its own record-keeping rules for supporting documents that I cannot confirm.

context_purpose: A fleet company wants evidence that a driver is experienced and reliable before waiving a deposit.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full account screenshots expose passenger names, addresses, daily earnings and phone number when two thresholds would do.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The company loses detail on cancellations, complaints and earnings stability, but trip count and rating are the stated criteria.

transmission_check.reason: The deposit waiver is the company's own commercial policy with no legal duty to hold screenshots.

context_purpose: A landlord or agent wants reassurance that a prospective tenant pays rent reliably and can cover a month's rent buffer.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full statements reveal counterparties, medical and family payments and salary source that go far beyond payment regularity.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A single-account aggregate cannot show other accounts, income level, or whether the payments were rent to a real landlord, so a landlord may still prefer fuller evidence.

transmission_check.reason: Tenant screening by private landlords is a choice, and I know of no duty to collect statements.
